theories.hypothesis: A recent progressive handicap chase winner can be worth opposing where a rise meets specific comparable chase evidence in the opposition; the rise alone is insufficient.
theories.mechanism: Changed effective terms may narrow a demonstrated form margin, while an established rival or claimant supplies a concrete winning route.
theories.scope: All 46 Saturday UK/Irish races screened in this review; final active favourite/joint favourite or close market leader in a handicap chase, latest completed race a chase win, higher handicap burden, and a named rival with comparable demonstrated chase evidence. Fix current eligibility now and record exclusions.

qualifying_candidates.note: Independent race qualification, not theory promotion.

theories.scope_exclusions: Rock My Way did not win his latest race; Realta Liath did not win latest; Chosen Hero’s latest win was a hurdle, not a chase; Steel Ally’s race is not a handicap. Flat and hurdle handicap winners are outside this version.
theories.counterargument: Both qualifiers can improve beyond their raised marks; reappearance form and course suitability can justify favouritism.
theories.limitations: Qualitative entry comparisons; no calibrated probabilities; jockey claims are not guaranteed ability gains; two differently selected groups must be shown separately.
theories.weakening_evidence: Repeated favourite wins despite favourable rival comparisons; failed direct-form reversals; net losses at the actual frozen prices; profit concentrated in few results or one condition.
theories.revision_policy: Retain v1 and prospectively date any changed definition; do not refit past results.

theories.evaluation_plan: Retain all eligible observations and revisions; track losing streaks, commission-adjusted P/L, profit concentration, actual winner/name/rank, conditions and observed withdrawals. Count each race once across overlapping tags. Require relevant repetition and a genuinely subsequent prospective batch before presenting complete evidence for possible future use. No universal sample size, confidence or automatic promotion threshold.

theories.hypothesis: A leading chase debutant may be opposable when multiple rivals have credible useful jumping ability and specific routes to transferring it to fences, while the favourite’s own transfer case remains consequential.
theories.mechanism: Alternative useful jumpers may translate proven hurdle/point ability sufficiently to beat the market-leading recruit; chase inexperience itself is not the mechanism.
theories.scope: All 46 Saturday UK/Irish races screened; active market-leading novice/beginners chase horse with no prior Rules chase start, useful own hurdle/point case, and at least one rival with useful established jumping evidence plus another specific supported route.
theories.scope_exclusions: Koktail Divin and Kiss Will already have chase form; Lulamba is NR and already has chase form; Lastbutnotleased runs over hurdles and Mister Boum in a bumper, outside this theory.
theories.counterargument: Mighty Park may be a much better chaser; opposition also has uncertain transfers.
theories.limitations: Only one present candidate; no causal proof or calibrated probability; do not interpret every chase debut defeat as validation.
theories.weakening_evidence: Favourite’s superior jumping/class decides the race, rivals fail to transfer or none of the named rivals supplies the anticipated mechanism; negative price-based P/L.
theories.revision_policy: Version changes prospectively; keep old outcomes and definitions.

theories.hypothesis: In maiden hurdles, demonstrated useful hurdle competition may be sufficient to oppose a market-leading bumper winner on hurdling debut at an independently accepted Lay quote.
theories.mechanism: Prior hurdle performance may translate to a more reliable winning route than the favourite’s still-unproven hurdle transfer, while the favourite can improve substantially.
theories.scope: All 46 Saturday UK/Irish races screened: maiden hurdle, active favourite or joint favourite a bumper winner with no previous hurdle start, and at least one rival with demonstrated relevant hurdle placing plus another supported hurdle route.
theories.exclusions: Lastbutnotleased is a point recruit, not a recorded bumper winner; The Walk is already a hurdle winner; novice hurdle winners, chases, Flat novices and bumpers are outside v1.
theories.counterargument: A festival bumper winner can have materially more potential than exposed hurdle opponents; the new trip can suit him.
theories.limitations: One proposed case; race type and qualitative comparison restrict generalisation; no calibrated probability or profitable-edge claim.
theories.weakening_evidence: Favourite’s jumping/ability comfortably surpasses named established rivals; beaten favourite owes defeat to an unanticipated newcomer rather than the proposed mechanism; adverse actual-price P/L or profits concentrated in few circumstances.
theories.revision_policy: Any revision receives a new version before future races; earlier cases remain exploratory unless contemporaneously frozen under this version.
